questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard very good about Taiwan as a destination and thought it sounded very exciting

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Medium-easy: the host university is very helpful and has very good information they will send beforehand, but sometimes there are some stuff that can be a bit confusing. But in that case I just asked the university and they were quick to assist and guide

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before I arrived, I was assigned a local student who was going to be my contact person and helper. He was so nice and helped with all the questions and troubles I had with courses, living accommodation and life in general in Taiwan. He even picked me up at the airport. We ended up becoming good friends also, went out with him and his friends a few times. But I don't all local students are that involved, other people I talked to had barely heard from their local student

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy, there are many different websites to find housing through (was recommended a long list by the host university). I used
https://myroomabroad.com/
as it seemed safe and reliable. Other people found housing through Facebook groups, but I was a bit afraid of getting scammed so I didn't do that. But it seems to be an option too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Prices are a bit higher compared to living on-campus but I would say it is definitely worth it: no restrictions on guests (on-campus residents can have guests staying overnight), more privacy, nicer rooms etc. The price of off campus housing is still really cheap compared to Copenhagen. I paid around 2500-3000 DKK per month

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: This is my one main complaint about my stay. The course registration was very chaotic and stressful to me. Before you arrive, you can sign up for courses. You will most likely not get enough to satisfy the credit requirement, so in the first week you have to go to the classes you want and ask the professor if you can sign up for their class. If the class isn't full, they will say yes, but you don't really know which classes are available otherwise.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Got help from the university and my local student

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got them all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The first week of class is a trial-week, where you can go to all the classes you are considering. If you want the class you ask the professor for a code to sign up. I went to all the classes I could to acquire codes, so I had as many classes to choose from as possible. It is kind of a puzzle calender-wise to make it all fit, so good to have all the options open. And if you don't want the class you just sign-off, quite easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Varied a lot from the easiest course I have ever done (felt like high school level) to the most difficult one (felt like PhD level)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Overall less group discussion and more lectures, but varies from class to class and professor to professor. I had some classes too that were very group-discussion based, and I liked it a lot

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Political Science (Ⅱ) (comparative politics)
Public Administration (Ⅱ).

KU didn't initially approve my forhåndsgodkendelse for Introduction to International Relations (Ⅱ) and Political Science (Ⅱ) as they thought it was too similar to DAK3 and IP. So be careful not to fall in the same trap.

questions.answer: Didn't see any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't see any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel Taiwan! The country is small and developed, so it is very easy to get around the entirety of the island with trains and busses. The nature of Taiwan is amazing, so travel as much as you can!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. There are some new customs to get used to (talked more quietly, not eating on trains, less physical contact like no hugging ever) but it comes quickly. The locals are also more forgiving towards you as a foreigner if you happen to break the customs, so don't worry

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very shy in approaching you (almost never happens) but they are so happy to interact and talk to if you establish connection. Their level of english varies a lot though

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How afraid of social contact many people are

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything is so convenient and runs smoothly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Travel Taiwan
Don't stress about school, you will do fine
Enjoy it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The nightlife is kinda underwhelming

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling around Taiwan

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Forhåndsgodkendelse

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
